title: Cross-Model Upgrade — Pareto Advancement, Equivalence Classes and Stop Rules
status: archive-generated research-governance formalization; comparison logic across heterogeneous models, not a shared physical law
abstract: The defect calculus introduced a typed vector of reconstruction, information, commutation, Door, contract and predictive failures. This upgrade defines how such heterogeneous defects should guide model advancement without being collapsed into an arbitrary single score. Models are compared only on a common target, dataset, validity regime and set of applicable diagnostics. After scaling each defect by a declared application tolerance, Pareto dominance identifies models that are no worse on every relevant diagnostic and strictly better on at least one while not paying an unacceptable complexity cost. Models on the Pareto frontier remain legitimate trade-offs; dominated models should be simplified, revised or retired. The result gives the project a formal stopping rule for equation growth: added ontology survives only when it moves a model onto or along a defensible advancement frontier.

required_common_context: same target observable or decision family
comparison_domain.rule: Do not numerically Pareto-rank unrelated domains; cross-domain use is methodological only.

tolerance_normalization.meaning: d_i<=1 places a defect within its declared tolerance; normalization does not make heterogeneous diagnostics physically identical.

pareto_dominance.definition: A dominates B when every applicable normalized defect is no worse, at least one is strictly better, and complexity cost does not increase unacceptably.
pareto_dominance.front: Nondominated models form the advancement frontier.
pareto_dominance.meaning: A richer theory does not survive merely by fitting one aspect better while becoming substantially less identifiable, robust or economical elsewhere.

observable_equivalence.definition: Models are practically equivalent for target O when output differences remain within a predeclared tolerance over the tested regime.
observable_equivalence.selection: Within an equivalence class prefer the lower justified complexity unless richer internal structure is independently measured or supports another declared task.

statuses.promoted: passes core tolerances and adds discriminating value
statuses.approximation_only: useful only in a bounded regime
statuses.nonclosed: declared state description omits generated structure or balance terms
statuses.observationally_redundant: simpler model is equivalent for the target
statuses.dominated: another model is no worse and better on at least one criterion
statuses.rejected_in_regime: violates a hard mathematical or empirical constraint

stop_rules: Stop adding parameters when the model is observationally redundant with a simpler member of its equivalence class.
Stop interpreting hidden mechanisms when the model is underidentified and no feasible measurement resolves the ambiguity.
Stop calling a system closed when brackets, balances or perturbation equations generate missing structure.
Stop promoting a model that is Pareto-dominated under the declared comparison context.
Retain negative and downgraded results because they constrain later theory construction.
new_project_principle: A theory should become harder to keep as it becomes more complicated. New structure earns survival by reducing a named defect, creating a successful new prediction, enabling an intervention, or compressing multiple results without losing identifiability and correspondence limits.
